question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-8, what is the minimum age to qualify as an applicant for a Georgia real estate salesperson's license?
choice_a: 18 years old
choice_b: 21 years old
choice_c: 19 years old
choice_d: There is no statutory minimum age, only an education requirement
explanation: Salesperson and community association manager applicants must be at least 18 years old, while broker and associate broker applicants must be at least 21.

question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-8(b), besides the age and instructional-hour requirements, what academic credential must a salesperson license applicant hold?
choice_a: A high school diploma or a certificate of equivalency (such as a GED)
choice_b: An associate's degree in any field
choice_c: A real estate-related college degree
choice_d: No academic credential is required by statute
explanation: Salesperson applicants must be a high school graduate or hold a certificate of equivalency, in addition to meeting the age, residency, course-hour, and examination requirements.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-8(b), how many instructional hours of Commission-approved salesperson prelicense coursework must an applicant complete before qualifying to take the salesperson's examination?
choice_a: At least 75 instructional hours
choice_b: At least 60 instructional hours
choice_c: At least 40 instructional hours
choice_d: At least 100 instructional hours
explanation: A salesperson applicant must furnish evidence of completion of at least 75 instructional hours in a Commission-approved salesperson's course of study, distinct from the 25-hour post-license course required after the license issues.

question: How does the statutory minimum age for a broker or associate broker applicant under O.C.G.A. 43-40-8(c) compare to that for a salesperson applicant under subsection (b)?
choice_a: Broker/associate broker applicants must be at least 21; salesperson applicants must be at least 18
choice_b: Both must be at least 21
choice_c: Both must be at least 18
choice_d: Broker applicants must be at least 18; salesperson applicants must be at least 21
explanation: Subsection (c) sets a higher 21-year minimum age for broker and associate broker applicants, while subsection (b) sets an 18-year minimum for salesperson applicants.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-8(c), a candidate for a broker's or associate broker's license must have maintained a salesperson's license in active status for what portion of the years immediately preceding application?
choice_a: At least three of the five years immediately preceding application
choice_b: At least one of the two years immediately preceding application
choice_c: All five years immediately preceding application
choice_d: At least two of the three years immediately preceding application
explanation: Broker and associate broker applicants must have maintained an active-status license for at least three of the five years preceding the application, in addition to the 60-hour broker's course and examination requirements.

question: Which of the following correctly matches the Commission-approved prelicense course hour requirement under O.C.G.A. 43-40-8 to the license type?
choice_a: Salesperson 75 hours; Broker 60 hours; Community Association Manager 25 hours
choice_b: Salesperson 60 hours; Broker 75 hours; Community Association Manager 25 hours
choice_c: Salesperson 75 hours; Broker 25 hours; Community Association Manager 60 hours
choice_d: All three license types require the same 60 hours
explanation: O.C.G.A. 43-40-8 sets a 75-hour prelicense course for salespersons, a 60-hour course for brokers/associate brokers, and a 25-hour course for community association managers.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-8, what is the general residency requirement for a Georgia real estate salesperson license applicant?
choice_a: The applicant must be a Georgia resident, unless the applicant qualifies under the chapter's nonresident licensure provisions
choice_b: The applicant must have resided in Georgia for at least five years
choice_c: There is no residency requirement of any kind
choice_d: The applicant must be a U.S. citizen residing in any state
explanation: Salesperson applicants must generally be Georgia residents, subject to the chapter's separate nonresident-licensure exception.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-8(a), what are the age and course-hour requirements for a community association manager applicant?
choice_a: At least 18 years old, with completion of at least 25 instructional hours in a community association manager's course
choice_b: At least 21 years old, with completion of 75 instructional hours
choice_c: At least 18 years old, with no education requirement at all
choice_d: At least 25 years old, with completion of 18 instructional hours
explanation: Community association manager applicants must be at least 18, be a high school graduate or equivalent, and complete at least 25 instructional hours in a Commission-approved CAM course.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-2, how does the Georgia Real Estate Commission select its chairperson?
choice_a: The Commission organizes by electing a chairperson from among its own members
choice_b: The Governor directly appoints the chairperson
choice_c: The Secretary of State appoints the chairperson
choice_d: The longest-serving member automatically becomes chairperson by statute
explanation: The Commission organizes itself by selecting a chairperson from among its own six members.
source_note: O.C.G.A. 43-40-2 (hedge: exact subsection letter not independently re-confirmed against primary statute text this session, though the quoted language was read directly)

question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-2, how often must the Georgia Real Estate Commission meet?
choice_a: At least once a month, or as often as necessary
choice_b: At least once a quarter
choice_c: At least twice a year
choice_d: Only when called by the Governor
explanation: The Commission must meet at least once a month, or as often as necessary, and may remain in session as long as the chairperson deems necessary.
source_note: O.C.G.A. 43-40-2 (hedge: exact subsection letter not independently re-confirmed against primary statute text this session, though the quoted language was read directly)

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-2, on what grounds may the Governor remove a Commission member, and what procedural protection applies?
choice_a: Inability or neglect to perform duties, incompetence, dishonest conduct, or licensing-agency sanctions -- only after notice and an opportunity for a hearing
choice_b: The Governor may remove any member at will, without cause or hearing
choice_c: Only a two-thirds vote of the other Commission members can remove a member
choice_d: Removal requires a criminal conviction of the member
explanation: The Governor may remove a Commission member for inability or neglect to perform duties, incompetence, dishonest conduct, or disciplinary sanctions from another licensing agency, but only after giving notice and an opportunity for a hearing.
source_note: O.C.G.A. 43-40-2 (hedge: exact subsection letter not independently re-confirmed against primary statute text this session, though the quoted language was read directly)

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-4, what is the role of the Georgia real estate commissioner within the Commission's structure?
choice_a: A full-time chief executive officer appointed by the Commission, which also sets the commissioner's salary
choice_b: A part-time volunteer position filled by the Commission's chairperson
choice_c: An elected position filled by statewide popular vote
choice_d: A position appointed directly by the Governor, independent of the Commission
explanation: The office of real estate commissioner is a full-time chief executive officer position; the Commission appoints the commissioner and sets the salary.

question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-4, what restriction applies to the real estate commissioner while serving in that office?
choice_a: The commissioner may not hold any interest in a real estate business or related enterprise while serving
choice_b: The commissioner must personally hold an active broker's license
choice_c: The commissioner may continue operating a private brokerage while serving
choice_d: There is no restriction on the commissioner's outside business interests
explanation: The commissioner is barred from holding an interest in a real estate business or related enterprise while serving, to avoid conflicts of interest.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-4(c), what must the real estate commissioner do upon assuming office?
choice_a: Take an oath to faithfully discharge the duties of the office
choice_b: Post a $50,000 surety bond
choice_c: Complete the 60-hour broker's prelicense course
choice_d: Submit to Senate confirmation
explanation: The commissioner must take an oath to faithfully discharge the duties of the office before assuming its powers.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, what is the maximum amount the Real Estate Education, Research, and Recovery Fund will pay per transaction, regardless of how many persons were aggrieved?
choice_a: $25,000.00 per transaction
choice_b: $15,000.00 per transaction
choice_c: $50,000.00 per transaction
choice_d: There is no per-transaction cap, only a per-licensee cap
explanation: The fund will not pay more than $25,000.00 per transaction, regardless of the number of persons aggrieved or parcels of real estate involved.

question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, at what aggregate dollar amount of court-ordered payments on behalf of one licensee does the fund's liability for that licensee terminate?
explanation: The fund's liability for the acts of any one licensee terminates once court orders have authorized an aggregate of $75,000.00 in payments on that licensee's behalf.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, what is the maximum amount any single claimant may ever obtain from the Recovery Fund?
explanation: No person who establishes a proper claim under this Code section may ever obtain more than $25,000.00 from the fund.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, what happens to a licensee's license when a court order authorizes payment from the Recovery Fund on that licensee's behalf?
choice_a: The license is automatically revoked
choice_b: The license is automatically suspended for 90 days
choice_c: Nothing happens unless the Commission separately votes to discipline
choice_d: The license converts automatically to inactive status
explanation: The license of a licensee for whose acts the fund pays a claim is automatically revoked upon the issuance of the court order authorizing that payment.

question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, once a licensee's license is revoked due to a Recovery Fund payment, under what condition can that person become relicensed?
choice_a: Only after repaying the fund in full, plus interest at the judgment rate
choice_b: After a mandatory two-year waiting period, with no repayment required
choice_c: Relicensure is permanently barred with no exception
choice_d: After completing an additional 36 hours of continuing education
explanation: A licensee whose license was revoked because of a Recovery Fund payment cannot be relicensed until the fund is repaid in full, plus interest at the judgment rate.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, what right does the Commission acquire after paying a claim from the Recovery Fund?
choice_a: The Commission is subrogated to the rights of the judgment creditor against the licensee
choice_b: The Commission gains no further rights once the claim is paid
choice_c: The Commission may only recover funds through a new licensing fee surcharge
choice_d: The claimant retains all rights, and the Commission has no recourse
explanation: Once the Commission pays a claim from the fund, it is subrogated to all the rights of the judgment creditor, who must assign the judgment's rights, title, and interest to the Commission.

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, if the Recovery Fund's balance falls below its statutorily required minimum, what may the Commission do with respect to renewal licensees?
choice_a: Assess an additional recovery fund fee of up to $30.00 per year at renewal
choice_b: Immediately suspend all active licenses statewide
choice_c: Double the standard renewal fee for every licensee
choice_d: Require licensees to personally guarantee the fund with a surety bond
explanation: The statute requires the Commission to maintain a minimum fund balance and permits it to assess renewal licensees up to $30.00 per year if needed to maintain that balance.
source_note: O.C.G.A. 43-40-22 (hedge: the minimum-balance and per-year assessment figures came from a secondary-source summary of the statute text rather than a directly-quoted primary excerpt; not independently re-verified against the raw code section this session)

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(1)(a)3, in addition to the renewal fee due, what fee applies to reinstate a license that lapsed for nonpayment of fees or failure to meet education requirements, if reinstated within four months of the date of lapsing?
explanation: If the lapsed license or approval is reinstated within four months of lapsing, the reinstatement fee is $100.00, in addition to the renewal fee due.

question: Per Rule 520-1-.04(1)(a)3, if a license is reinstated more than four months after lapsing, what additional fee applies beyond six months from the lapse date, for an individual licensee versus a firm or school?
choice_a: $100.00 plus $25.00 per month (individual) or $50.00 per month (firm/school) for each month or partial month beyond six months from the lapse date
choice_b: A flat $500.00 regardless of how many months have passed
choice_c: $25.00 per month for both individuals and firms, with no distinction
choice_d: The license cannot be reinstated after four months under any circumstances
explanation: If reinstatement occurs more than four months after lapsing, the fee is $100.00 plus an additional $25.00 per month (individual/instructor) or $50.00 per month (firm/school) for each month or partial month beyond six months from the lapse date.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(1)(a)4, a $25.00 fee applies for which of the following failures?
choice_a: Failing to notify the Commission in writing within 30 days of an address change, opening or closing a trust account, transferring to a new firm, or going on inactive status
choice_b: Failing to complete continuing education by the renewal deadline
choice_c: Failing to display a wall certificate of licensure at the licensee's place of business
choice_d: Failing to pay the Recovery Fund portion of the activation fee
explanation: A $25.00 fee applies for failing to give the Commission timely written notice within 30 days of an address change, opening/closing a trust account, transferring to a new firm, or failing to affiliate or apply for inactive status within 30 days as required.

question: Per Rule 520-1-.04(1)(a)5, what fee does the Commission charge for a check submitted to it that is returned unpaid, or for a credit card charge that is disputed and results in a chargeback?
explanation: The Commission charges $100.00 for a returned check or for a credit card dispute that results in a chargeback to the Commission's account.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(1)(a)6, an approved instructor's or school's original approval activation and renewal fee covers all fees due until what date, unlike an individual license, which runs to the licensee's birth month?
choice_a: December 31st in the fourth calendar year following the year the approval was granted
choice_b: The anniversary date of the approval, every year
choice_c: June 30th in the third calendar year following approval
choice_d: There is no fixed renewal cycle for schools and instructors
explanation: An instructor's or school's original approval fee covers all fees due to the Commission until December 31st in the fourth calendar year following the year the approval was granted.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(3)(a), how must the Commission determine the passing score for its licensing examinations, and when must the methods and score be published?
choice_a: By psychometrically sound criterion-related methods assessing minimal competence, published prior to the exam's administration
choice_b: By a fixed statutory 75% cutoff published only after each exam administration
choice_c: By majority vote of the Commission after each testing cycle, unpublished
choice_d: The passing score is set solely by the testing vendor with no Commission involvement or publication requirement
explanation: Candidates must make a passing score determined by psychometrically sound criterion-related methods associated with assessment of minimal competence, and both the methods and the minimum passing score must be published before the exam is administered.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(3)(c)-(d), a candidate disabled in the line of duty during qualifying service whose disability is rated below 10 percent at the time of the exam is entitled to how many preference points, as distinguished from a candidate rated at 10 percent or above?
choice_a: Five points, versus ten points for a rating of 10 percent or above
choice_b: Ten points, the same as a rating of 10 percent or above
choice_c: Three points, versus five points for 10 percent or above
choice_d: No points unless the rating reaches at least 10 percent
explanation: A disabled candidate whose service-connected disability is rated below 10 percent is entitled to five preference points, while one rated at 10 percent or above is entitled to ten points.

question: Per Rule 520-1-.04(3)(e), veterans preference points on the licensing examination never apply to a candidate who lacks what?
choice_a: An honorable discharge
choice_b: A minimum of two years of total service
choice_c: A service-connected disability rating
choice_d: Georgia residency at the time of discharge
explanation: Veterans preference points never apply to a candidate who has not been honorably discharged, regardless of otherwise qualifying service.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(3)(f), to qualify for veterans preference points, a candidate must have served in a branch that participated in the relevant conflict, served at least how many days during a formally declared war or authorized campaign, and submit proof through what channel?
choice_a: At least 90 days, with proof submitted on official forms available through the Veterans Administration or Department of Defense
choice_b: At least 30 days, with proof submitted via a notarized personal affidavit only
choice_c: At least 180 days, with proof submitted directly to PSI
choice_d: There is no minimum day requirement, only an honorable discharge
explanation: The candidate must have served at least 90 days of active duty in a branch that participated in the relevant war or conflict, and must submit proof of service on official forms available through the Veterans Administration or Department of Defense.

question: Per Rule 520-1-.04(3)(b)-(d), when a qualifying candidate for a broker's license receives veterans preference points, to which parts of the broker exam are those points added, as opposed to a salesperson or community association manager candidate?
choice_a: To the Information Gathering section grade and the Decision Making section grade, rather than to the candidate's overall answer grade
choice_b: To every section equally, identically to salesperson and CAM candidates
choice_c: Points are not available to broker candidates at all
choice_d: To the national portion of the exam only, never the state portion
explanation: For a broker candidate, veterans preference points are added to the grade made on the Information Gathering section and to the grade made on the Decision Making section, rather than to the overall answer grade used for salesperson and CAM candidates.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(3)(i)-(j), what consequence can follow from an examinee, licensee, approved instructor, or approved school improperly sharing or obtaining information about the content of a Commission qualifying examination?
choice_a: Grounds for denial of license or the imposition of any sanction permitted under O.C.G.A. 43-40-25, which may also apply to instructors and schools
choice_b: A civil fine only, with no effect on licensure or school/instructor approval
choice_c: No consequence unless the sharing is proven to have caused another candidate to pass
choice_d: Automatic criminal prosecution with no administrative option
explanation: Improperly supplying or obtaining qualifying-exam content is grounds for denial of license or for imposing any sanction permitted by O.C.G.A. 43-40-25, and can also be grounds against approved instructors and schools.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(3)(k), absent written Commission permission, when may a person take a qualifying examination the Commission offers?
choice_a: Only to qualify for or reinstate the license the exam is designed for, to satisfy another state's reciprocity requirement after being licensed in Georgia by reciprocity, or when ordered by the Commission in a disciplinary matter
choice_b: At any time, for practice purposes, with no restriction
choice_c: Only once per calendar year regardless of purpose
choice_d: Only if sponsored by an approved school
explanation: Without written Commission permission, a person may take a qualifying exam only to qualify for/reinstate the applicable license, to satisfy another state's reciprocity requirement after being licensed in Georgia by reciprocity, or when required by a Commission disciplinary order.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(3)(g), a candidate moving to Georgia may be licensed without further examination or education upon producing certification showing which four things about the candidate?
choice_a: Passed an examination for that license type, met all prelicense and continuing education requirements of the other state, is licensed in good standing at certification, and has had no disciplinary action imposed by that state's licensing body
choice_b: Only that the candidate currently holds an active license, with no other conditions
choice_c: That the candidate has practiced real estate for at least ten years
choice_d: That the candidate passed the Georgia state-specific examination remotely
explanation: The certification must show the candidate passed an exam for that license type, met the other state's prelicense/continuing education requirements, is licensed in good standing at certification, and has had no disciplinary action -- otherwise the candidate must take and pass the Georgia qualifying exam.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(4)(b), what determines the effective filing date of an application or fee mailed to the Commission, and who bears the burden of proof if it is received after a deadline?
choice_a: The United States Postal Service postmark date, if mailed -- and the applicant or licensee bears the burden of proving timely filing if receipt is late
choice_b: The date the Commission physically opens the envelope, with no burden on the applicant
choice_c: The date the applicant printed the application, regardless of mailing
choice_d: There is no defined effective date; all deadlines are based on receipt only
explanation: The effective filing date is the USPS postmark date if mailed, or the date the Commission dates receipt if otherwise filed; if receipt comes after the deadline, the applicant or licensee bears the burden of proving timely filing.

question: Per Rule 520-1-.04(4)(d), what can render an application 'incomplete,' and what can failing to disclose a required criminal conviction on it constitute?
choice_a: Missing the proper fee, required documents, requested data, signatures, or legible responses makes it incomplete; failing to disclose a required conviction may constitute a falsified application
choice_b: Only a missing signature can make an application incomplete; nondisclosure of convictions has no separate consequence
choice_c: Incompleteness is defined solely by a missing photograph
choice_d: There is no such thing as an incomplete application under the rule
explanation: An application is incomplete if it lacks the proper fee, required documents, requested data, signatures, or legible responses; failing to disclose every criminal conviction as defined by O.C.G.A. 43-40-15(a) may constitute a falsified application.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(4)(f), how and by when must a candidate with a disability request a reasonable examination accommodation?
choice_a: In writing, received in the Commission's office by the application deadline, with appropriate supporting documentation
choice_b: Verbally, at the PSI testing center on exam day
choice_c: There is no accommodation process; the ADA does not apply to licensing exams
choice_d: By email only, with no deadline
explanation: A disability accommodation request must be made in writing, received in the Commission's office by the application deadline, along with appropriate supporting documentation.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(2)(b), when an out-of-state jurisdiction cannot certify a broker candidate's active-status experience, what other credible evidence may the Commission consider?
choice_a: Transaction files reflecting brokerage activity, an affidavit from a currently licensed broker the applicant was affiliated with, or the candidate's own affidavit corroborated by affidavits from three other brokers
choice_b: Only a notarized letter from the candidate's spouse
choice_c: Only tax returns showing real estate commission income
choice_d: No alternative evidence is ever accepted; the application must be denied
explanation: The Commission may consider transaction files, an affidavit from a currently licensed broker who can attest to the applicant's affiliation and activity, or, if the candidate was a broker, the candidate's own affidavit plus affidavits from three other corroborating brokers.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(12), if the Commission denies a license application after the applicant met all age, education, examination, and fee requirements, within how many days must the applicant request a formal hearing, or the application lapses?
choice_a: 60 days
choice_b: 30 days
choice_c: 10 days
choice_d: 90 days
explanation: The applicant must request a formal hearing in writing within 60 days of the Commission's mailed denial notice; failing to do so causes the application to lapse, requiring the applicant to reapply and retake any required exam.

question: Effective July 1, 2017, under Rule 520-1-.04(13), what benefit is available to military spouses and transitioning service members applying for a Commission license?
choice_a: Expedited processing of the license application
choice_b: A full waiver of all licensing fees
choice_c: Automatic licensure without any examination
choice_d: An extended two-year window to complete prelicense education
explanation: Military spouses and transitioning service members may qualify for expedited processing of any license application, provided they show that status and otherwise meet the applicable fee and licensure requirements.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(11), what is the legal effect of a Commission 'preliminary decision' on an individual's prior conviction or disciplinary action, made before that individual becomes a license applicant?
choice_a: It is merely advisory guidance and not binding, though a favorable preliminary decision may become the Commission's final decision without further investigation or hearing once the individual applies
choice_b: It is a final, binding, and appealable order the moment it is issued
choice_c: It automatically disqualifies the individual from ever applying
choice_d: It has no effect on any future application and must be requested again from scratch with no carryover
explanation: A preliminary decision provides advisory guidance and is not binding, but the Commission may allow a favorable preliminary decision to become its final decision without further investigation or hearing when the individual later applies.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(8), a candidate, applicant, or licensee who reveals a reportable criminal conviction must supply the Commission with certified copies of what two documents?
choice_a: The citation, accusation, information, or indictment that led to the conviction, and a certified copy of the sentence
choice_b: A police incident report and a character reference letter
choice_c: Only a personal written explanation of the incident
choice_d: A bar association clearance letter and proof of restitution
explanation: The person must supply the Commission with a certified copy of the citation, accusation, information, or indictment that led to the conviction, and a certified copy of the sentence.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(9), a candidate, applicant, or licensee who reveals a prior disciplinary action by another licensing agency must supply the Commission with certified copies of what?
choice_a: Any allegations that preceded the final order, and the final order itself
choice_b: Only a summary letter from the other agency
choice_c: Nothing further is required beyond disclosing that the action occurred
choice_d: A signed waiver of confidentiality only
explanation: The person must supply certified copies of any allegations that preceded the final order, plus the final order itself, from the other licensing agency's disciplinary action.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(6)(a), what must a broker operating as a sole proprietor supply to the Commission regarding the firm's name?
choice_a: The name in which the broker intends to conduct business, which is then shown on the broker's certificate of licensure
choice_b: A registered fictitious-name affidavit filed with a court
choice_c: Nothing; sole proprietors are exempt from any firm-name requirement
choice_d: A name pre-approved by the Secretary of State's trademark division
explanation: A sole proprietor broker must supply the Commission with the intended business name on the license application, and that same name is shown on the broker's certificate of licensure.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(6)(b), if a corporation applying for a broker's license wishes to conduct business under a trade name, what must it additionally submit with its application?
choice_a: A certified copy of its trade name, certified by the Clerk of the County in which the trade name certificate is on file
choice_b: A copy of its federal EIN confirmation letter
choice_c: A notarized statement from every corporate officer
choice_d: Proof of trade name registration with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office
explanation: A corporation wishing to conduct business under a trade name must submit a certified copy of its trade name, certified by the Clerk of the County where the trade name certificate is on file, in addition to its corporate charter.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(6)(d), what must a limited liability company applying for licensure as a broker submit with its application?
choice_a: A copy of its certificate of authority to transact business in Georgia as issued by the Secretary of State's office
choice_b: A copy of its federal partnership tax return
choice_c: A surety bond equal to its authorized capital
choice_d: A copy of its operating agreement notarized by all members
explanation: An LLC applying for broker licensure must submit a copy of its certificate of authority to transact business in Georgia, issued by the Secretary of State's office.

question: Under Rule 520-1-.04(6)(e), how must a franchisee's trade name on a broker license application be structured relative to other firms registered with the Commission?
choice_a: It must include both the franchise name and either the firm's own charter/agreement/authority name or a distinct trade name registered in each county where it does business, so it can be discerned from other firms
choice_b: It may consist of the franchise name alone, with no distinguishing information required
choice_c: Franchisees are prohibited from using the franchise name in any firm name
choice_d: The franchise name must be omitted entirely from the Commission's records
explanation: A franchisee's trade name must include the franchise name plus either the firm's own charter/partnership/authority name or a distinct county-registered trade name, so it can be reasonably distinguished from other Commission-registered firms.

question: How does O.C.G.A. 43-40-1 statutorily define a 'salesperson,' as distinguished from an associate broker?
choice_a: Any person, other than an associate broker, who acts on behalf of a real estate broker in performing any act authorized by the chapter
choice_b: Any licensed individual who owns their own independent brokerage
choice_c: A person who exclusively manages community association services
choice_d: A person licensed only to perform ministerial acts, never negotiations
explanation: A 'salesperson' is defined as any person, other than an associate broker, who acts on behalf of a real estate broker in performing any act the chapter authorizes -- distinguishing the role from an associate broker, who holds broker-level qualifications but affiliates with another broker.
source_note: O.C.G.A. 43-40-1 (hedge: exact paragraph number not independently re-confirmed against primary statute text this session)

question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-1, the term 'licensee' encompasses which categories of Commission-issued licenses?
choice_a: Community association manager, salesperson, associate broker, and broker
choice_b: Only broker and associate broker
choice_c: Only salesperson and community association manager
choice_d: Any person who has ever taken the licensing exam, whether licensed or not
explanation: 'Licensee' is defined to mean any person licensed by the Commission as a community association manager, salesperson, associate broker, or broker.
source_note: O.C.G.A. 43-40-1 (hedge: exact paragraph number not independently re-confirmed against primary statute text this session)

question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-1, how is a 'ministerial act' statutorily defined?
choice_a: An act related to real estate brokerage activities that a licensee or the licensee's employee performs without requiring discretion or the exercise of the licensee's own judgment
choice_b: Any act that generates a commission for the licensee
choice_c: An act that only a broker, never a salesperson, may lawfully perform
choice_d: An act requiring the exercise of professional judgment on the client's behalf
explanation: A 'ministerial act' is an act related to real estate brokerage activities performed by a licensee or the licensee's employee that does not require discretion or the exercise of the licensee's own judgment -- this is the category of service a broker may still provide to a mere 'customer' who has not entered a brokerage engagement.
source_note: O.C.G.A. 43-40-1 (hedge: exact paragraph number not independently re-confirmed against primary statute text this session)
